description: A game played in the Netherlands in medieval times, possibly a precursor to modern golf.
A golf-like stick and ball game played in the streets during medieval times.
A common scoring system where the player with the lowest total strokes after 18 holes wins.
A format where two players or teams compete hole by hole, with the winner having the most holes won.
A scoring system where points are awarded based on performance per hole rather than total strokes.
A team-based format where players choose the best shot and all play from that position.
A game where each hole has a prize, and the player who wins the hole outright wins the prize.
A variation of golf where players aim to complete the course in the fewest strokes and fastest time.
A short version of golf played on a course with holes typically less than 80 yards long, requiring only pitching and putting.
A putting-only version of golf played on artificial surfaces, often with obstacles.
A variation of Mini-Golf played on a pool table using pool cues.
A putting-style game where balls are hit into a small goal rather than into a hole.
A competition to determine who can hit a golf ball the farthest.
A golf variation where players aim at a net and score points based on landing position.
A winter version of golf played on snow and ice.
A summer version of golf played on sand with a lightweight foam ball.
An indoor version of golf where shots are made into a screen that simulates the course.
Golf played in urban areas with various obstacles and unconventional terrains.
A simplified golf variation from Japan, played with a single club and ball.
A croquet variation where players take turns hitting a ball through hoops.
A Danish sport combining croquet and golf, played by hitting a ball into a hole with a mallet.
A golf variation where players throw a frisbee into a chain basket as the hole.
A sport where competitors try to take the fewest throws to propel a metal ball along country roads.
A German sport where participants throw a ball to reach a target area in as few throws as possible.
An indoor game where a ball is hit with a putter into holes on a pool table.
A pocket billiards game where players pocket nominated balls in order using pool cues.
A word game where players link two words by changing one letter at a time, invented by Lewis Carroll.
